IPC channel contract in packages/desktop/src/shared/types/ipc.ts (currently one-way typed, unknown[] args)
renderer<->engine document content contract (markdown string + sanitized selection/history/TOC shapes) currently scattered in editor.vue
engine type boundary @muyajs/core (permissive any via types/muya-core.d.ts shim)

rationale: The answer is a strong, evidence-grounded architecture review. It classifies the repo from multiple independent signals (Electron deps, BrowserWindow/ipcMain usage, sandbox config, electron-vite) and correctly identifies macOS/darwin as the host while treating the legacy muyajs engine as retired, not current. Its ~12 core evidentiary claims were verified: sandbox settings and webSecurity:false in config.ts; one-way-typed IPC contract with 108 bare ipcMain.on/handle across 23 main-process files and zero contract-type imports; dual channel families plus the ipcMain.emit internal-event hack (internalIpc.ts and ~40 emit call sites); closed WindowType; engine any-boundary via muya-core.d.ts; editor.vue adapter layer (adaptSelectionChange/CONTAINER_FUNCTION_TYPE/SyntheticHistory/ag-vs-mu DOM); dual document truths reconciled via json-change/file-changed; versioned atomic buffer-store; scattered file-workflow responsibilities; and a disconnected legacy engine. It explicitly resolves the two documentation-vs-implementation drifts (CLAUDE.md sandbox claim and ARCHITECTURE.md pre-monorepo layout) by relying on implementation evidence and flagging the docs as stale, so both drift entries are decision-relevant but resolved. All nine dimensions are met at full credit: ranked quality attributes with explicit trade-offs and verification; three viable options including the status-quo hardening; a recommendation that follows from the stated drivers (one active engine, two window types, one local file backend); and an incremental, individually-revertible migration with per-step exit criteria and concrete tests. Five minor factual imprecisions remain (bufferedState.ts path, WindowType member count, E2E/unit test counts, an unsupported 'Tauri adapter' aside, and the handleClose hardcoding attribution) but none is material and none relies on stale documentation for a decision, so the accuracy gate passes.
